newsitem.title: UK: INSIGHT -T-bonds to struggle at 112-13 resistance.
newsitem.headline: INSIGHT -T-bonds to struggle at 112-13 resistance.

text.p: The outlook for September T-bonds remains constructive, but near term they will struggle to get through 112-13 resistance, technical analysts said on Thursday.
Sam Malone-Jansens, an analyst on the futures desk at Lloyds Bank Futures in London, said that level was the first resistance pivot point with a second point above there at 112-22.
"In Japanese candlestick terms a tweezer bottom was formed on June 17, 18 at 111-17 and that ensures the uptick," he said.

"As far as momentum goes slow Stochastics are currently trading around 90.14 pct," he added. "Historic one-year highs are around this level so I'm a little concerned the market may run out of steam quite soon."
By 0929 GMT, September T-bonds were unchanged at 112-05.
Malone-Jansens said before 111-17 came into play there was a tighter congestion support level at 111-26.
"The larger picture is looking very good and realistically the eventual attainment of that isolated high from February 18, at 113-09, is the target."
He said hourly charts showed that when T-bonds spiked up from the 111-17 bottom, the reaction upwards was very steep.

"In five hours the market spiked up to 112-08 and since then it has gone sideways so effectively you have a potential flag formation which normally errs towards a temporary pause prior to the market extending yet again," he said.
"So on a daily basis stay long of this market given a non-violation of 112-01/02 and trade the upside."
Donna Liu, technical analyst at DKB International in London, said she was "cautiously bearish" on the market.
"The top of the two and a half month uptrend is at 112-16 and if the market can't get through that, the short term outlook is negative," she said.
She put immediate support at 111-24, then 111-17, the daily lows from Tuesday and Wednesday.
By 1005 GMT, September eurodollars were unchanged at 94.150 and the December contract was at 93.960, also unchanged.
